title: Per-request observability snapshot and replay for low-overhead tracing
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Build a lightweight per-request observability snapshot and replay mechanism used by SDKs and middleware to maintain trace/metadata fidelity across asynchronous boundaries, worker handoffs, and retry flows without imposing heavy allocations or blocking hot paths. The feature should: capture minimal context (trace id, sampling hint, short provenance stamp, selected baggage keys, pointer to cached KV entries), serialize into a compact token (<128 bytes when possible), and allow downstream replay to rehydrate SDK-internal state (span parentage, sampling decision, important tags) and attach telemetry to the correct logical request. This solves duplicated or orphaned spans seen in background worker handoffs, mitigates missing parent spans on SDK retries, and provides a mechanism for safe reattachment when using prefix/KV caches.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Node, Python, Go) can produce a compact snapshot token on request entry and consume it to rehydrate in a different execution context or process
End-to-end integration test reproduces previously observed orphan span case and shows spans are correctly parented after replay
P50 request latency overhead < 1% on synthetic benchmark with high-concurrency load; memory overhead per request < 200 bytes (median)
Snapshot token format versioned and backward-compatible; header name negotiated with feature flag (x-rd-snap-v1)
implementation_notes: Design doc: drive/Redwood/obs/per-request-snapshot-v1 (internal) — prototype format proposals and failure modes
Snapshot fields: trace_id (16B), span_id (8B), sampling_byte (1B), provenance_hash (4B), baggage_kv_list (varint-encoded), kv_cache_refs (varint list of short indices)
Encoding: use base64url of a compact binary where possible; SDKs fall back to JSON in environments where binary headers are restricted

SDK changes: Node -> AsyncLocalStorage capture + coordinator that writes header and returns token; Python -> contextvars + lightweight C-extension helper for binary encoding; Go -> context.Context helper and middleware for net/http and grpc interceptors
Sampling: respect upstream sampling decision; include sampling hint to allow deterministic downstream decisions without additional RPCs
KV cache integration: store short reference IDs for commonly cached prefixes to avoid duplicating payloads; coordination with runtime cache index endpoint (runtime idx API) required
Failure modes: token corruption should be treated as missing token (no crash); we will add strict size checks and a telemetry counter for token-parse-failures
Privacy: do not include PII; only allow RDC-allowed baggage keys configured via SDK options
Feature gating: enable behind org feature flag and per-route opt-in via Redwood Console rollout policy
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting with SDK owners (Node, Python, Go) and Observability team. Agreed on minimal field set and versioned header approach.

2026-02-22: Prototype in Node SDK demonstrates snapshot token ~84 bytes for typical request (trace+span+sampling+baggage(2 keys)+2 cache refs). Benchmark harness shows ~0.4% P50 overhead at 2k RPS test.

2026-03-03: Cross-language format alignment call — Python to adopt binary format using built-in base64url encode path; Go to expose compact builder API. Added a short provenance_hash to detect cross-service reparenting anomalies.

2026-03-08: PR drafts: github.com/redwood/sdk-node/pull/312 (snapshot encoder + middleware), github.com/redwood/sdk-go/pull/178 (context helper + http middleware). Early review feedback: prefer explicit opt-in for baggage whitelist and ensure token size guard.

2026-03-12: Integration test harness updated to simulate worker handoff via SQS; replay logic successfully rehydrates parent span in 92/100 trials. Remaining: add resilience for partial KV index misses and finalize rollout plan.
risks_and_mitigations: Header size limits on some proxies could truncate tokens — mitigation: SDKs detect truncation (missing expected delimiter) and fallback to sending only trace_id header and increment telemetry counter
Legacy clients without SDK update will not emit tokens — ensure runtime can still correlate using existing sticky attributes and fallback sampling
Binary header incompatibility across language SDKs — use base64url and publish strict spec and tests; add roundtrip conformance suite
Performance regressions under high concurrency — run 24h soak on dedicated perf cluster; revert to sampling-only mode if overhead > 2% observed
testing_plan: Unit tests: encoder/decoder roundtrip across Node/Python/Go implementations
Integration tests: worker-handoff scenario with SQS/Kafka, HTTP retry flows, and background job runners
Perf tests: 1k/5k/10k RPS synthetic workloads comparing no-snapshot vs snapshot with typical baggage
Chaos tests: simulate truncated token, token-parse errors, and KV-index miss to verify graceful degradation
Canary rollout: 10% of traffic in staging orgs using feature flag, escalate to 50% after 48h metrics look stable
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy SDK-only change to emit snapshot header when opt-in flag is enabled (behind console toggle). No runtime changes required.
Stage 2: Enable runtime decoding on a small subset of frontend proxies to validate parse-success rate and token size distribution.
Stage 3: Enable replay in worker pool services and background processors with strict guard rails (max token size, parse limit)
Stage 4: Full rollout with monitoring dashboards for parse-failures, overhead, and parentage-fix rate
dashboards_and_alerts: New dashboard: 'Snapshot Token Health' — key charts: tokens emitted per service, parse success rate, token size distribution (P50/P95/P99), token-parse-error rate
Instrument metric: obs.snapshot.reparented_spans.count (how many spans were reattached by replay) to measure value
Add annotation to latency dashboard to show rollout windows and correlate with P50/P95 regressions
next_steps: Finish PR feedback items (baggage whitelist, size guard) and submit final reviews — assigned to Marco Ruiz
Add cross-language conformance tests to CI so any SDK change that breaks decoding fails pipeline
Coordinate runtime index endpoint to publish stable short ids for KV cache prefixes (ENG-43902 planned dependency)
Prepare canary config in Redwood Console and schedule 72h monitoring window post-canary
